summary.text: Adrian Dowell is the One Nation candidate for Monbulk at the 2026 Victorian election. According to the ABC's guide he is a registered building inspector who earlier worked in construction, logistics and car repair, and he has lived in several parts of the electorate. One Nation's candidate page could not be read (it refuses automated requests), and we found no other published biography as at early November 2026.

sources.title: Monbulk: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Alyssa Wormald is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Monbulk at the 2026 Victorian election, having stood for the party in Bayswater in 2022. A long-time wildlife campaigner, she founded the Australian Native Parrot Protection Association and is president of the Victorian Kangaroo Alliance. She works in university administration and, with her sister, runs a small business making vegan, eco-friendly burial shrouds.

occupation.text: University administration; co-owner of an eco burial products business

prior_roles.organisation: Heaven and Earth Eco Burial Products

priorities.text: Ending the lethal control of native parrots and kangaroos
Opposing duck shooting
Opposing the proposed Montrose Quarry expansion

summary.text: Clare Fitzmaurice is the Liberal candidate for Monbulk at the 2026 Victorian election. Trained as a physiotherapist, she later moved into public policy, and since November 2024 she has advised the federal Nationals MP Anne Webster. The party describes her as a mother of three raising her family in the Dandenong Ranges.

prior_roles.role: Policy adviser to Anne Webster MP
Public policy roles in national advocacy organisations
prior_roles.note: Sources mention this work without naming the organisations or saying when it ended

priorities.text: Easing cost-of-living pressure on households
Better emergency services
Improving local roads

sources.title: Monbulk: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Clare Fitzmaurice, Liberal for Monbulk, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Craig Manners is the Family First candidate for Monbulk at the 2026 Victorian election. He is chief executive of Orbus Ministries Australia, a charity working with communities in Malawi, and has spent more than 40 years in finance, mining supply and charity management. He stood for Family First in Aston at the 2025 federal election, polling 2.7 per cent, and has been a Senate candidate for the party.

prior_roles.role: Small business manager supplying the mining and drilling industries

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC says he has stood for the Senate for Family First but gives no year. Wikipedia lists a Craig Manners third on Family First's Victorian Senate ticket in 2016 (the earlier Family First Party); not confirmed to be him.

priorities.text: Lower cost of living and much lower taxes
An inquiry into corruption in the unions and the Labor Party
Tougher action on crime, including graffiti
Deregulating housing and land
Refocusing schools on core subjects

sources.title: Monbulk: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Craig Manners, Candidate for Monbulk, Family First Party Australia
Results of the 2025 Australian federal election in Victoria, Wikipedia
Candidates of the 2016 Australian federal election, Wikipedia

summary.text: Daniela De Martino has been Labor's member for Monbulk since 2022, when she succeeded the retiring MP James Merlino. She has been an Acting Speaker since February 2024 and Secretary to the Parliamentary Labor Party since June 2026. Before Parliament she taught in secondary schools, worked as a union industrial officer and ran an organic grocery. She is recontesting Monbulk in 2026.

occupation.text: Owner of an organic grocery store; earlier a secondary teacher and union industrial officer

prior_roles.role: Secretary to the Parliamentary Labor Party
Owner and manager of an organic grocery store
prior_roles.note: The Parliament biography says she ran it for more than six years until March 2022.

prior_roles.organisation: Shop, Distributive and Allied Employees Association
prior_roles.note: The Parliament biography gives no years.

prior_roles.role: Secondary school teacher (English, History and Geography)

priorities.text: Education
The environment
Health care
Helping small businesses offer good, secure jobs

sources.title: Daniela De Martino, Parliament of Victoria

summary.text: Dr Merran Blair is the Greens candidate for Monbulk at the 2026 Victorian election. A dietitian by training, she lectures at Monash University and grew up in the Dandenong Ranges. She ran for the Greens in the federal seat of Casey in 2025, taking about 11 per cent of the first-preference vote.

priorities.text: I want to be a strong and sensible voice for our electorate
Stronger climate action, given the hills' exposure to climate-related disasters
Policies that deliver affordable housing
Politics that does not give way to corporations and billionaires

summary.text: Noah Briggs is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Monbulk at the 2026 Victorian election. He works as a paralegal, holds a law degree from Deakin University and volunteers with the Eastern Community Legal Centre. His campaign centres on taxing billionaires and large companies to pay for public services and housing.

priorities.text: no one should be denied the things we need to live a good life
Higher taxes on billionaires and big corporations to fund public services
Guaranteed affordable housing, including for people waiting on social housing lists
Holding energy companies to account over prices and long outages after emergencies

sources.title: Monbulk: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
